trial_court: Family Court in HMA Case No. 788/2010
case_name: Jag Parvesh Singh vs Manjeet Kaur
facts_of_case: Marriage between the parties was solemnised on 16.05.2004. The respondent joined her matrimonial home at Rampura, Delhi. Due to temperamental differences and estrangement, they started living separately. The appellant preferred a petition under Section 13 (1) (i-a) of the Hindu Marriage Act on the ground of cruelty.

legal_principles.principle: Procedural sin should never be the death of rights.
legal_principles.held: The processual law so dominates in certain systems as to overpower substantive rights and substantial justice. The humanist rule that procedure should be the handmaid, not the mistress, of legal justice compels consideration of vesting a residuary power in Judges to act ex debito justitiaie where the tragic sequel otherwise would be wholly inequitable.
cited_cases: Kumar Sen Vs. State of Bihar : AIR 1975 SC 1185

legal_principles.principle: The ultimate guardian of justice should be the Judge.
legal_principles.held: Parliament, I hope, will consider the wisdom of making the Judge the ultimate guardian of justice by a comprehensive, though guardedly worded, provision where the hindrance to rightful relief relates to infirmities, even serious, sounding in procedural law.
cited_cases: Kumar Sen Vs. State of Bihar : AIR 1975 SC 1185

outcome.final_order: The impugned Ex-parte Judgment/Decree dated 16.07.2013 passed by the Family Court was set aside.
